title: GenomicsChain extension to an IEEE 2791 BioCompute Object
description: The object held under `genomicschain_extension` in an `extension_domain` entry whose `extension_schema` is this URL. Written by gc_prov_write (producer or enricher) and read by the genomicschain_prov adapter (design docs/design/prov_anchoring_design_v0_1.md §4, §13.4-1, §6.1, §6.2). Every value is the producer's own statement; GenomicsChain's record re-derives what it can from the bundle bytes and lists the rest as not_checked. NOT YET PUBLISHED at its URL: publishing is the operator's decision, before anything is sold (§6.1 (5)).

producer.description: What wrote this block. A bundle whose blocks name different producers records neither.

checksums.description: SHA-256 of the bytes behind a locator, joined to inputs, outputs, tools, the runtime and workflow scripts by the exact locator string. The standard's own field is SHA-1; this carries SHA-256 beside it. Two different digests for one locator pin nothing.

platform.description: What the computation ran on, as the producer states it (design v0.1.12 §6.1 (2)). Never the host name.

zk_receipts.description: RISC Zero receipts covering named steps (design v0.1.12 §6.1 (3)). The receipt file stays with its producer; this declares its fingerprint and what its journal binds. A ZK receipt shows only that the named steps were computed correctly from the recorded inputs. It covers only those steps and does not show that the recorded inputs are the raw data.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the receipt file (bincode-serialised risc0 Receipt)

image_id.description: guest image ID: the 32 digest bytes (eight u32 words, little-endian) in hex

journal.description: journal = risc0 serde of ([u8;32], Vec<u8>): (SHA-256 of the step's input file, the step's output bytes)

input_uri.description: a locator in that step's input_list, with a SHA-256 in checksums[]

output_uri.description: a locator in that step's output_list, with a SHA-256 in checksums[]

resources.description: The computing resources of the run (design v0.1.14 §6.2): the machine the bundle writer examined or the customer states, and each stage's requested and observed values with where they came from. Self-reported (not_checked resources_as_written). Graded on its own scale (gc-resources-0.1), not part of the overall grade. Of these values, only GPU vendors and models (filtered) reach the record, beside three closed-vocabulary fields derived from the bundle (machine_source, resources_sources, gpu_vendors_probed); CPU model, memory, disk and per-stage values stay in the bundle. Never a host name, user, serial, UUID, MAC or PCI bus id.

machine.description: The machine the bundle writer ran on (source probe) or the one the customer states (source plan). Not necessarily what a task could use: a container on macOS cannot reach the host GPU.

disk_free_bytes.description: bytes free on the disk holding the working directory, when written

gpu_probe.description: Each GPU probe tried and how it ended. The vendors a probe covers are fixed by its name (nvidia-smi: nvidia; rocm-smi: amd; system_profiler: amd, apple, intel).

gpus.description: One entry per GPU. Written only when a probe answered or the customer states it: [] means looked for and none; no key means not looked for.

steps.description: Per-stage values, any number of entries per stage (one per job, per source). A reader takes the largest requested value, the largest peak memory, run time and CPU percent, and the sum of bytes read and written.

observed.description: Measured by a tool; a plan does not state these.
